items.title: Section: Does Meditatively Produced Matter Include Smell and Taste? A Second Round of Scholarly Debate

items.zh: 復次，法處所攝勝定果色中，當知唯有顯色等相。何以故？於彼香等生因闕故，又無用故。如是於空行風中無有俱生香等，唯有假合者。又離輪外所發光明，所餘大種及與香等皆不可得。又法處所攝勝定果色，當知此色唯依勝定，不依大種。然從緣彼種類影像三摩地發，故亦說彼大種所造；非依彼生，故名為造。
items.en: Furthermore, within matter subsumed under the mental sense-field and produced through meditative mastery, one should know there is only the characteristic of visible colour and the rest. Why? Because the causes generating smell and the rest are lacking there, and because there is no use for them. Likewise, within wind moving through space, there is no inherently co-arisen smell, only what is temporarily borrowed. And apart from its source, emitted light lacks the remaining elements and smell and the rest altogether. Furthermore, matter subsumed under the mental sense-field and produced through meditative mastery depends only on meditative power, not directly on the elements — yet since it arises from concentration upon an image resembling that category, it is also said to be produced by those elements, though not directly generated from them, hence it is called "produced."

items.title: Section: Visible-and-Obstructive, Invisible-and-Obstructive, Invisible-and-Unobstructive — Establishment's Close

items.zh: 問：於色蘊中，幾法由有見有對故住？幾法由無見有對故住？幾法由無見無對故住？答：一由二種，謂眼所行；餘唯有對；除法處所攝色，當知此色無見無對。如是等類，應當思惟色蘊安立。
items.en: Question: within form aggregate, how many phenomena exist as visible and obstructive? How many as invisible yet obstructive? How many as invisible and unobstructive? Answer: one, of two kinds, namely what the eye perceives; the rest are merely obstructive; excluding matter subsumed under the mental sense-field, one should know this matter is invisible and unobstructive. Things of this kind are how form aggregate's establishment should be contemplated.

items.title: Section: Continuity — Three Kinds of Flow, and Four Ways Ripened Matter Keeps Changing

items.zh: 復次，色蘊由幾種流而相續轉？謂由三種。一、等流流，二、異熟生流，三、長養流。初等流流，復有四種。一、異熟等流流，二、長養等流流，三、變異等流流，四、本性等流流。
items.en: Furthermore, by how many kinds of flow does form aggregate continue in succession? By three kinds: the flow of concordant continuation, the flow of karmic ripening, and the flow of nourishment. The first, concordant continuation, is further of four kinds: ripening-based continuation, nourishment-based continuation, transformation-based continuation, and nature-based continuation.

items.title: Section: Karmic Ripening and Nourishment — Twenty Thousand Recitations to Calm the Mind, and Continuity's Close

items.zh: 異熟流者，復有二種。一者、最初，二者、相續。謂業生異熟，及異熟所生。謂即從彼業力所引異熟，後時轉者。長養流者，亦有二種。一、處寬遍長養流，二、相增盛長養流。初長養流，唯色長養；當知由食、睡眠、梵行、等至長養諸色。餘長養流，當知亦由食故、彼所依故、修勝作意故、長時淳熟故而得長養。諸有色法，由二長養之所長養；諸無色法，唯相增盛說名長養。又欲界色，具由四食，及餘一切長養因緣而得長養；色界諸色，不由段食、睡眠、梵行而得長養。又諸色根，當知由二種流而得流轉。以諸色根離異熟、長養相續流外，無別等流流。問：異熟相續，有時亦有增長廣大可得，何故異熟攝流非即長養耶？答：由別有長養相續能攝能持異熟等流流故，現有增長等。若非根所攝色，當知具三種流。諸心心所有等流流、異熟生流、第二長養所長養流。法處所攝色，無異熟生流；餘如心心所應知。又欲界中，具有內外諸色成熟。於色界中，遠離香、味。又欲界中，諸色根成熟或具不具。於色界中，必具諸根。又諸聲界亦有異熟，非聲。如是等類，應當思惟色蘊流義。
items.en: The flow of karmic ripening is of two kinds: initial and continuing... the flow of nourishment is also of two kinds: growth in extent and growth in vigour... the pure sense faculties flow through only two kinds of flow... non-faculty matter possesses all three kinds of flow... matter subsumed under the mental sense-field has no karmic-ripening flow; the rest should be understood as with mind and its mental factors... the desire realm possesses both internal and external matter in maturity; the form realm lacks smell and taste... the sound-element also has a ripening continuity, though not sound itself. Things of this kind are how form aggregate's meaning of flow should be contemplated.

items.title: Section: Five Functions Each for Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind — Then Five More for Whatever They Produce

items.zh: 復次，色蘊所攝地界能為幾業？乃至風界能為幾業？當知一切皆為五業。謂地界能為打觸變壞業、建立業、與依止業、違損業、攝受業。水界能為流潤業、攝持業、溉灌業、違損業、攝受業。火界能為照了業、成熟業、燒然業、違損業、攝受業。風界能為發動業、隨轉業、消燥業、違損業、攝受業。又諸大種於所生造色，當知能作五業。謂生起業、依止業、建立業、任持業、增長業。
items.en:
Furthermore, how many functions can the earth-element within form aggregate perform? And so on up through the wind-element — how many functions can it perform? One should know all perform five functions each. The earth-element can strike and break, build, provide support, cause harm, and nurture growth. Water can moisten, bind, irrigate, cause harm, and nurture growth. Fire can illuminate, ripen, burn, cause harm, and nurture growth. Wind can set in motion, accompany motion, dry out, cause harm, and nurture growth.
Furthermore, the elements, with respect to the derived matter they produce, are able to perform five further functions: a generative function, a supportive function, an establishing function, a sustaining function, and a growth function.

items.zh: 於彼變異生時，能為導首故。變異生已，與彼為處不相捨離，能為依止故。攝受、損害安危共同，能建立彼故。持彼本量令不損減，故能任持。令彼積集增進廣大，故能增長。

blocks.text: The analysis of matter continues: what kind of form meditation produces, how form flows on, and what the elements do.

It has only the mark of visible colour and the like; smell and taste lack causes and use. Master Cháng Bǎi: water manifested in absorption does not come from the water element; it arises from concentrating on an image of water, and so is called "produced by the elements" only in a loose sense.

Visible and obstructive (what the eye sees); invisible but obstructive (the rest); invisible and unobstructive (form as a mental object). Master Cháng Bǎi: form manifested in absorption is of the last kind.
Master Cháng Bǎi: form differs moment by moment yet continues in similarity; the water ahead resembles the water behind, but what was seen a moment ago is not what is seen now.
Growth in extent and growth in vigour. Master Cháng Bǎi: the body need not grow larger; it can become stronger and more lustrous.

Each element has five functions, the last two always harming and nurturing. Master Cháng Bǎi: water too benefits beings and the world. Derived form shares safety and danger with the elements, because it is established by them.
"What was seen a moment ago is not what is seen now." A river, a face, a body: each is a continuity, not a thing.

quiz.q: Why does the form produced by absorption have no smell or taste?
options: the causes producing smell and taste are lacking and there is no use for them; there is only the mark of colour and so on
smell and taste belong to solid food, which absorption has cut off, so they merely fail to arise for the time
the power of absorption falls short, and only a buddha's can manifest them
such form is wholly unreal, and so has nothing at all
quiz.why: The treatise says that this form has only the mark of visible colour and the like, since the causes of smell and the rest are lacking and there is no use for them. Master Cháng Bǎi: the conditions for smell and taste are incomplete, and they would have no function. The same reasoning appears in the form realm's lack of smell and taste.

quiz.q: Form of absorption does not depend on the elements. Why is it still called produced by them?
options: it arises from absorption on an image of that kind; water in absorption is manifested by its power, not born of water, so it is "produced," not "generated"
because it is in fact generated directly by the elements, "not depending" being a manner of speaking
because the meditator's body is made of the elements
because 造 is a copyist's error for 生
quiz.why: The treatise says it arises from concentration on an image of that category, and so is said to be produced by the elements, though not generated from them. Master Cháng Bǎi: water manifested in absorption does not come from the water element but from the power of absorption; so it is not called generated from water but produced by it.

quiz.q: What in form is visible and obstructive, invisible yet obstructive, and neither?
options: form under the mental sense-field is visible and obstructive; what the eye perceives invisible and unobstructive; the rest merely obstructive
all form is visible and obstructive, since all form has resistance, the treatise's distinction being a difference of wording
the elements are visible and obstructive; derived form neither
what the eye perceives is visible and obstructive; the rest merely obstructive; form under the mental sense-field invisible and unobstructive
quiz.why: The treatise answers that one class has both features, namely what the eye perceives; the rest are merely obstructive; and form under the mental sense-field is invisible and unobstructive. Master Cháng Bǎi: form manifested by absorption cannot be seen and has no obstruction. The English "one, of two kinds" may mislead: it means one class possessing both marks.

quiz.q: The English has "the flow of natural continuation" for 等流流 and "the flow of karmic ripening" for 異熟生流. How do they fare by the lecture?
options: 等流 is similar continuation from one moment to the next, not "natural"; the 生 of 異熟生流 goes unrendered
等流 is the flow of a river, "natural" meaning the natural world, so the English is exact and needs no comparison with the lecture
等流 is a flow of equality, and should be "equal flow"
異熟生流 is good and evil karma, and should be so rendered
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: form differs from moment to moment, yet continues in similarity; the water ahead resembles the water behind, but what was seen a moment ago is not what is seen now, though ordinary beings take it as the same. So 等流 means similar continuation. "Natural continuation" misses this, and it is confusing beside "nature-based continuation" for 本性等流流.

quiz.q: How do growth in extent and growth in vigour differ in the flow of nourishment?
options: the first is appearance growing strong; the second is space taken up enlarging, both occurring only in the form realm
the first is the space taken up enlarging; the second is the size unchanged while the appearance grows strong, lustrous, and vigorous
the first is good karma growing; the second is evil karma growing
the first is the world expanding; the second is lifespan lengthening
quiz.why: The treatise lists growth in extent and growth in vigour. Master Cháng Bǎi on the second: the size or space taken by the form aggregate has not grown, but its appearance has become strong, lustrous, and vigorous. The non-form aggregates take up no space and so have no growth in extent. Most of the treatise's account of these flows is absent from the English.

quiz.q: Which two functions are common to earth, water, fire, and wind?
options: causing harm and nurturing growth
building and providing support
illuminating and ripening
setting in motion and accompanying motion, since all four move things along
quiz.why: The treatise gives each element five functions, the last two always being causing harm and nurturing growth. Master Cháng Bǎi: water too has the function of benefiting beings and the world. So each element can both harm and help. The other options are functions proper to a single element, such as illuminating and ripening for fire.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say of the elements' generative function towards derived matter?
options: the elements change first and derived matter then alters, its change having them as forerunner
derived matter changes first and the elements follow, taking it as forerunner, and hence the name generative function
the elements and derived matter change separately, wholly unrelated
the elements never change, only derived matter does
quiz.why: The treatise lists five functions: generative, supportive, establishing, sustaining, and growth. Master Cháng Bǎi: the four elements change first, and derived matter then alters, the change of the elements leading the change of derived matter. This is why the seed account does not cancel the claim that the elements produce derived matter.

quiz.q: 建立業 is "build" for earth and "an establishing function" towards derived matter. Is this double rendering good here?
options: good: for earth it means constructing, towards derived matter sharing fate, and the senses really differ, which the English keeps apart
bad: both should read "build," for the sense is identical and the English makes a needless distinction
bad: both should read "destroy," 建立 being ironic
bad: neither Chinese passage has 建立, both being additions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: derived matter shares safety and danger with the four elements, because it is established by them; whatever changes occur, it does not leave them. That is not the same as earth building things in the world. So the English pair "build" and "establishing function" marks a real difference; not every double rendering is a fault, and here it helps.
